events.details: tues 6pm (monthly thru 12/1):: sit onstage with virtuoso musicians during columbia university school of the arts's hour-long early-evening concerts, with a free drink in hand and the opportunity to mingle with the performers afterward. the 15th season continues tonight with pianist conrad tao, performing the premiere of david fulmer's i have loved a stream and a shadow , a solo piano work inspired by the poetry of ezra pound. miller theatre at columbia university (morningside heights), free admission.

events.title: Scientific Controversies: Octopus Umwelt
events.description: for the latest installment of pioneer works' scientific controversies series, comparative psychologist and marine biologist dr. alex schnell ( national geographic: secrets of the octopus ) and dr. caroline albertin inves...
events.details: tues 7pm doors:: for the latest installment of pioneer works' scientific controversies series, comparative psychologist and marine biologist dr. alex schnell ( national geographic: secrets of the octopus ) and dr. caroline albertin investigate what the octopus can reveal about the nature of consciousness, perception, the origins of the mind, and what it means to be intelligent. hosted by barnard physics and astronomy professor and pioneer works director of sciences janna levin. food will be available for purchase, and stargazing with the amateur astronomers association will precede and follow the event. pioneer works (red hook), free admission (donations welcome).
